source_name: NLB Banka Kosovo — Pasqyrat financiare (audited financial statements)
why_relevant: Dedicated audited-financial-statements section, separate from the annual-report section, with per-period entries (31.12.2021, 31.12.2022, 31.12.2023 observed). Separating statements from narrative reports makes this an unusually clean structured-extraction target for capital adequacy and NPL data.

source_name: NLB Banka Kosovo — Qëndrueshmëria (sustainability / non-financial disclosure)
why_relevant: Non-financial/ESG disclosure track of a systemic bank; ESG and sustainability statements often carry forward-looking strategy and product signals that do not appear in the audited statements.

source_name: NLB Banka Kosovo — Ankande publike (public auctions / collateral sales notices)
why_relevant: Public auction notices for repossessed collateral are a bank-published, high-frequency indirect indicator of loan-book stress and NPL workout activity — a leading signal that precedes the annual audited NPL figure.

source_name: BKT Kosova (Banka Kombëtare Tregtare Kosovë) — audited IFRS statements and annual reports
why_relevant: BKT Kosova publishes full IFRS audit reports as standalone PDFs on its own domain (2018 and 2023 files directly observed), alongside narrative annual reports. 100%-owned by BKT sh.a. Albania, so group-level reporting gives a cross-check.

source_name: Banka Ekonomike — Të dhënat financiare (financial data / annual reports)
why_relevant: Domestically-owned bank with a deep public archive of annual reports (2003 through 2023 observed), giving an unusually long time series for a Kosovo private bank — valuable for structural/market-share trend work.

source_name: Banka për Biznes (BpB) — Raportet financiare
why_relevant: Domestic SME-focused bank publishing independent auditor reports plus the CBK-format ('BQK') financial statements — i.e. both IFRS and supervisory-template disclosures, which is rare and useful for reconciling regulator aggregates to bank-level data.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Kosova — Pasqyrat Financiare (quarterly TM1-TM4)
why_relevant: Publishes financial statements on a QUARTERLY basis (labelled TM1-TM4) back to roughly 2015 — the most granular own-channel cadence found in the cell, enabling intra-year balance-sheet tracking for a Turkish-owned entrant.

source_name: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo — Raportet financiare / Financial statements
why_relevant: TEB is a top-tier Kosovo bank (BNP Paribas / TEB joint venture heritage) and this is its own disclosure page. Notably thin in search indexes — the documents appear to be reachable only from the page itself, so it must be crawled rather than searched.

source_name: İŞBANK Kosova (Türkiye İş Bankası A.Ş. — Kosovo branch/subsidiary) website
why_relevant: One of the licensed Kosovo banks; own-channel disclosures were not surfaced by search, so the site itself is the only candidate entry point. Smallest-tier player but relevant for market-entry and Turkish-capital-footprint analysis.

source_name: PriBank Sh.A. — corporate website
why_relevant: Newest/smallest licensed Kosovo commercial bank; its own site is the only plausible own-channel disclosure point. Searches returned no reports, so the disclosure surface is currently an open question rather than a confirmed absence.

source_name: CBK/BQK — Upustva za izveštavanje banaka, MFI i NBFI (Serbian-language supervisory reporting instructions)
why_relevant: Defines the reporting templates and IFRS/CBK framework that bank-published 'BQK' statement sets are built from — the schema key for parsing bank disclosures consistently across institutions. Confirms the regulator maintains a full Serbian-language track (?lang=sr), which is the entry point for sr-language coverage of this cell.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës (Kosovo Banking Association)
why_relevant: Sector body whose membership list is a second actor map and whose positions/communiqués often precede individual banks' public statements on fees, regulation and sector strategy. Its own domain was not confirmed by search; a member bank's page about it and its Facebook page are the confirmed handles.

source_name: ARBK — Kosovo Business Registration Agency / Gazeta Zyrtare filings
why_relevant: Because Kosovo's banks are unlisted joint-stock companies, shareholder-assembly decisions, capital increases and ownership changes are registered here rather than announced through a stock exchange. This is the substitute for an exchange-disclosure feed, and the Law on Business Organizations published via ARBK defines what a bank must convene and publish.

source_name: Parent-group investor relations as a proxy for Kosovo subsidiaries (RBI, NLB Group, ProCredit Holding, BKT Albania, İşbank, Ziraat)
why_relevant: Six of the ten Kosovo banks are foreign-owned subsidiaries. Parent groups — several of them listed and therefore subject to real securities-disclosure duty — publish segment data, strategic intent for the Kosovo/SEE market, and capital allocation decisions months before or in more detail than the local subsidiary. This is the highest-quality substitute for the investor-relations layer Kosovo's private banks structurally lack.

source_name: The Banker Database — TEB Bank Kosovo institution reports
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator holding standardised bank-level financials for Kosovo institutions; useful as a cross-check and gap-filler where a bank's own channel (notably TEB) is thin or unindexed. Paywalled, so treat as a licensed purchase decision rather than a scrape target.

source_name: Wikipedia — List of banks in Kosovo (actor-map pointer)
why_relevant: Fast, machine-readable roster mapping every licensed commercial bank to its official domain (PriBank, Banka Ekonomike, BKT, BpB, NLB, ProCredit, Raiffeisen, TEB, Ziraat, İşbank) — the seed list used to build this cell's crawl targets. Secondary to the CBK register for authority, but far easier to parse.

source_name: Centralna banka Republike Kosova (BQK/CBK) — Serbian-language site (?lang=sr)
why_relevant: The Kosovo central bank publishes its annual reports, financial stability reports, payment-system documents, regulations and press releases in a full Serbian-language mirror. This is the only authoritative primary regulator disclosure available in sr, and it is the legal basis for the euro-only cash payment regime that reshaped payments in Serb-majority areas.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — statements and media Q&A on Kosovo dinar/payment measures
why_relevant: NBS is the counterparty institution to the dinar-cash question and issues formal statements on the prevention of dinar inflow/use in Kosovo, on payment of salaries/pensions/social transfers, and on the banking-standards framing of the dispute. Primary institutional disclosure that no Pristina source reproduces.

source_name: KoSSev — north Kosovo Serbian-language news portal
why_relevant: Primary independent outlet based in north Mitrovica; covers bank branch closures, ATM/card availability, Poštanska štedionica operations, and CBK enforcement actions at a granularity no national or English source matches. Frequently reproduces bank customer notices verbatim.

source_name: Radio Kontakt Plus (Kosovska Mitrovica)
why_relevant: Mitrovica-based broadcaster reporting on bank branch operations, EU/international reactions to closures of Banka Poštanska štedionica units, and day-to-day payment access for the Serb community. Publishes bank service notices (ATM/e-banking availability) that document channel usage on the ground.

source_name: Radio KIM (Čaglavica/Gračanica)
why_relevant: Covers central-Kosovo Serb enclaves rather than the north, giving a second geography for banking access, pension/salary payout logistics and cash-vs-card behaviour. Also acts as a pointer: aggregates Radio Kontakt Plus and other Serb-community outlets.

source_name: Kosovo Online — Serbian-language Kosovo portal, economy section
why_relevant: High-volume sr-language desk dedicated to Kosovo affairs with a standing economy vertical; carried CBK currency decisions, bank statements and Belgrade institutional reactions. Useful for near-real-time monitoring of announcements affecting payment rules.

source_name: Danas — economy desk, Kosovo dinar/payments coverage
why_relevant: Belgrade daily with sustained analytical coverage of the dinar abolition, its effect on payment flows to Serbs in Kosovo, and proposals such as a Serbian financial organisation operating in Kosovo. Quotes named economists — useful for sourcing expert actors into the actor map.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL) — Balkan Service, Kosovo economy/currency reporting
why_relevant: Editorially independent sr-language service that reports both Pristina and Belgrade institutional positions on dinar import bans and CBK decisions, with document citation. Strongest counterweight to the partisanship of the other sr-language outlets in this cell.

source_name: Banka Poštanska štedionica a.d. Beograd — corporate/disclosure site
why_relevant: The Serbian state bank that operated the branch network serving Serbs in Kosovo (budget payouts: pensions, salaries, social transfers) and whose units in four northern municipalities were closed by Kosovo police. Its own disclosures and budget-payment product pages document the parallel payment channel directly.

source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka (Serbia) — customer notices on Kosovo/Metohija branch network
source_subtype: commercial bank corporate site / customer notices
why_relevant: Serbian commercial bank that historically ran branches in Kosovska Mitrovica and issued formal customer notices about closing its Kosovo/Metohija ekspozitura network and about card/e-banking migration. First-party evidence of a bank's exit from a market segment.

source_name: Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju, Vlada Srbije
why_relevant: Serbian government body issuing official statements on financial measures affecting Serbs in Kosovo — bank closures, payout arrangements, dinar transfers. Institutional primary source for the Belgrade side of parallel-system finance.

source_name: PIO Fond / Politika reporting on pension payouts at administrative crossings
source_subtype: national daily; reports state fund (PIO) figures
why_relevant: Documents the workaround payout mechanism (cash disbursement at four administrative crossings, ~28k beneficiaries) after in-Kosovo dinar payouts were blocked — a concrete, quantified description of a parallel payment arrangement that appears in almost no English-language source.
